row.notes: mov rdx,[rsp+0x60] in Sess_InGameRace_Update (+0x77e): the return address of the driver name fill call at 0x142d624e9 (0x14249ac60, jmp 0x14cb8a5d0). From here the game reads only the result string: rdx = [rsp+0x60], its character pointer, then mov qword [rsp+0x38],0, lea rcx,[rsp+0x38], xor r8d,r8d, xor r9d,r9d and call 0x1441974e0 (makes the message's driver name value from the characters); rax and the flags are first read after that call, so the name fill's return value (rax = the result address, 0x14cb8a7bb) is never read. Resuming here from site_Sess_InGameRaceRetirementDriver skips add rcx,0x18, lea rdx,[rsp+0x50] and the call: no push, pop or rsp change between the two sites and the callee-saved registers (rdi, rsi, rbx, rbp, r12-r15) keep the values the call preserves. The skipped name fill writes only its result at rsp+0x50..+0x97 (on the fallback path +0..+0x18) and reads the driver; the guard writes the same fallback result before it resumes. No branch lands in 0x142d624e1..0x142d624ed (linear sweep of 0x142d61d70..0x142d6308b); 0x142d624ee is reached only by the call's return. Resume target of the race retirement driver guard; not hooked or patched.
